elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Retained text reads "Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year". A calendar-year cap is not a rolling 12-month cap: a December inspection and a following January inspection are both permitted. To meet the preferred element the drafter would need "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The edit inserts "upon at least 15 days' notice" — half the preferred quantum, and it is not expressed as written notice.
Clause says only "at reasonable times"; no express business-hours limitation was added.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: "open for inspection by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio" — independent third-party auditor, subject to Customer's reasonable acceptance.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 4.4 contains no confidentiality undertaking from or in respect of the accountant, and the redline adds none; no non-disclosure obligation is imposed on the auditor in operative language.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No location/off-site language appears in the rendered clause; the books are simply "open for inspection".

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection", with reimbursement by Corio only "if any such inspection reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%) for the period under audit" — exactly the preferred cost allocation and threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is confined to inspection of "books of accounts and records for determining the amounts payable" by an accountant; no remote or direct system-access right is granted anywhere in the clause, so the walk-away trigger is absent.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year" — an express annual frequency cap satisfying the fallback (which does not require a rolling 12-month measure).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 replaces open-ended "reasonable notice" with "upon at least 15 days' notice", fixing a hard minimum notice period exactly at the fallback quantum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection", with cost-shifting only on an underpayment "of more than five percent (5%)". Vendor-borne cost is expressly allocated and the shifting trigger is the 5% figure the playbook itself specifies at the preferred level, so the cost-allocation element is satisfied; note the retained 5% (rather than 10%) trigger shifts cost to Customer somewhat sooner than the fallback figure if the team wants to press it.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: frequency (once each calendar year) and Vendor-borne cost with a 5% underpayment trigger were already in Section 4.4, and the single gap — an indeterminate "reasonable notice" with no floor — is closed by the inserted "at least 15 days' notice".

Preferred level is not reached: notice is 15 rather than 30 days and not stated to be written; there is no business-hours limitation (only "at reasonable times"), no off-site preference, no auditor confidentiality undertaking, and the frequency cap is calendar-year rather than any rolling 12-month period. These are correctly noted rather than pressed, but the level must not be marked complete.

Minimal: exactly one phrase is changed within the notice element ("upon reasonable notice" -> "upon at least 15 days' notice"). Favourable retained language — annual cap, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to Customer, Vendor cost-bearing, books-and-records-only scope, the reciprocal shortfall/overpayment true-up and the 3-year retention period — is untouched, and no survival tail, procedure or extra requirement outside the checklist is added.

Preserves intent: the audit's purpose (verifying amounts payable), the reciprocal payment/refund mechanic and the 5% reimbursement trigger all survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and "at reasonable times" still coexists coherently with the new fixed notice period.

Optional hardening if the counterparty engages: add "written" before notice and, if the team wants literal fallback parity on cost, raise the reimbursement trigger from 5% to 10%; neither is required for fallback completeness as scored here.

Severity is reduced to low: the clause sat at or above the fallback on every material term except the notice floor, and the walk-away triggers (unlimited/unannounced audits, system access) were never present.
